stimulus.text: Alexander Hamilton, Report on Public Credit, January 1790: “A national debt, if it is not excessive, will be to us a national blessing.” Paraphrase: Hamilton proposed that the federal government pay the national debt at full value and take over the states’ war debts, funding both by selling government bonds.
stimulus.source_note: Alexander Hamilton, Report on Public Credit, January 1790. Public domain.

source: original; stimulus quotes Hamilton, Report on Public Credit, January 1790, public domain.

primary_sources: Alexander Hamilton, Report on Public Credit (January 1790)

stem: Hamilton’s plan to fund the national debt at full value most directly benefited which group?

options.text: Speculators who had bought up old debt certificates at a fraction of their value.
Farmers who had sold their certificates to buy seed and tools.
options.misconception: The first holder is not always the one paid; the payment goes to the current holder.

options.text: Soldiers who still held the pay certificates they were given during the war.
options.misconception: Holding a certificate at the start is not the same as holding it when it is paid.

options.text: State governments that had already paid off their own war debts.
options.misconception: Assumption meant paying other states’ debts too, so a state that had paid its own did not gain.

rationales.A: Background: certificates had changed hands at a fraction of their value, so full payment gave the buyers a large gain.
rationales.B: Background: farmers who sold early received only the low sale price, not the full value.
rationales.C: Background: few soldiers still held their certificates; most had sold them for far less.
rationales.D: Background: states that had already paid their debts opposed paying other states’ debts.
rationales.general:
1. The stimulus says Hamilton would pay the national debt at full value.
2. Background: many original holders had sold their certificates cheaply because they doubted the government would ever pay.
3. Full payment therefore paid the buyers, who had bought low, the whole face value.
4. So the largest gain went to the speculators holding the paper, not to the soldiers who first earned it.
Remember: when a debt is paid at full value, ask who holds the paper now, not who held it first.
